name: Hahon
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog shows only Ross 1988 subgrouping; no descriptive grammar/phonology of Hahon located

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic languages. Richmond: Curzon.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Hahon appears only in the North-West Solomonic language list (pp. 883-884), with no sketch and no source cited for it.

sources.citation: Logan, Stephen. 2014-2016 (deposit). Documenting Hahon, an endangered language of the autonomous Region of Bougainville, P.N.G. ELAR deposit dk0305 / ELDP IGS0220, University of Newcastle (Australia). https://www.elararchive.org/dk0305/; collection hdl 2196/00-0000-0000-0009-E3A5-9
sources.note: Landing page contents list (verbatim items): 'for 25% of the recordings, detailed phonetic, phonological and morphological annotations'; 'Hahon-English/English-Hahon dictionary'; 'PhD thesis on grammar and dialectology in Hahon'; 'conference presentations and journal articles'. The visible item list (24 bundles) contains only recordings, transcriptions, life histories, dialect surveys and a 'Depositor's Metadata' bundle; no grammar, thesis or phonology document could be opened. Nothing about stress is visible.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell. 2005. The languages of Bougainville. In Anthony J. Regan & Helga M. Griffin (eds), Bougainville before the conflict, 31-46. Canberra: Pandanus Books / ANU E Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Lists 'Hahon (Hanon), NW Bougainville, 1,300 [1977]' (p. 36) and dialect/alternate names Kurur, Ratsua, Aravia (p. 37); Saposa/Taiof, Hahon, Tinputz and Teop are closely related (p. 34, citing Ross 1988: 217).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page haho1237 (Hammarström et al.), references: Ross 1988 (pp. 215-256) and Campbell et al. 2022 ElCat
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive reference at all (0 grammar/phonology/sketch entries); AES status Threatened. Confirms the earlier scan classification.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: RSPAS, ANU. (Glottolog ref 98107; the only Glottolog reference for Hahon, pp. 215-256)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988) (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing for Hahon. Chapter 7 (North-West Solomonic) gives Hahon only in consonant-correspondence tables (pp. 219-222) and lexical reflexes; data source for Hahon is listed as 'SIL' (p. 409); fn. 78 (p. 421) says Hahon retains final a and o but loses final i and u. All 'stress' hits in the book concern Ali/Schouten languages (pp. ~118-119), not Bougainville.

sources.citation: Lincoln, Peter C. 1976. Austronesian languages: Bougainville Province. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 419-439. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the chapter (0 hits). Hahon appears in the lexicostatistical matrix (Timputz family: Teop, Hahon, Timputz), a consonant-reflex chart, and notes on loss of *l and *ng > n (approx. pp. 423-431).

sources.citation: Lincoln, Peter C. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: Bougainville Province. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, 197-222. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Section 4.2.10.4.3 HAHON (p. 205) lists the entire prior record: 'Blackwood (1935): Hahon mentioned as group and located on map. Oliver (1949): Hahon. Allen and Hurd (1965): Hahon, Mr Busus. Capell (1971): Hahon.'

sources.note: The SIL survey that first recorded Hahon (wordlist from 'Mr Busus'); SIL survey reports of this era sometimes include a note on stress placement per language. Glottolog's only other Hahon reference.

sources.citation: Logan, Stephen. [year unverified, c. 2019-2023]. PhD thesis on the grammar and dialectology of Hahon. University of Newcastle (Australia); supervisor presumably Bill Palmer. Announced in ELAR deposit dk0305 contents as 'PhD thesis on grammar and dialectology in Hahon'.
